entries.name: Cable Row
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: seated at the cable row with the feet planted and the knees bent up-forward, the spine exactly 24 units and the neck exactly 9; the hands ride a long reach to the low pulley and pull to the ribs by driving the elbows back, the elbows solved on the exact shoulder circle. No database media row exists under this name; the standard seated setup was drawn (listed in the daily review). Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Six drawn positions of a cable row, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Start with long arms and the shoulder blades reaching forward.
Drive the elbows back to start the pull.
Elbows past the ribs; the upper back finishes.
Pause with the torso still.
Return the reach slowly.
Full reach again, torso tall and quiet.

entries.name: Band Row
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: standing tall with the band running from a chest-height anchor to both hands; the hands travel from a long reach toward the ribs with the elbows leading back, and the band visibly stretches through the pull. No database media row exists under this name; the standard chest-height anchor was drawn (listed in the daily review). The hands now reach the body: the torso is the vertical line at x 44.5, and the pulling position comes to within 3.0 of it, against 8.5 before, so the frames named for reaching the ribs and the neck now actually do. The elbow is solved on the shoulder circle from the authored hand, so the upper arm (12.5) and forearm (12.0) hold their length by construction. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Six drawn positions of a band row, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Start with both arms reaching long toward the anchor.
Drive the elbows behind you to start the pull.
Elbows past the ribs; the upper back finishes.
Pause with the torso tall and quiet.
Return the reach slowly.
Full reach again, tension still on the band.

entries.name: Cable Rope Rear-Delt Rows
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: seated tall at a low cable with the rope reaching forward at shoulder height; the pull drives the elbows wide and back to the upper chest, the rope ends separating at the finish. No database media row exists under this name; the standard low-cable rope setup was drawn (listed in the daily review). Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Six drawn positions of a cable rope rear-delt row, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Reach forward at shoulder height with the rope held in both hands.
Drive the elbows wide toward the back wall.
Keep the elbows wide through the finish.
Rope at the upper chest; the rear shoulders finish.
Pause with the torso tall and quiet.
Return wide along the same path.
Reach the shoulder blades forward again.
Full reach again at shoulder height.

entries.name: Low Pulley Row To Neck
entries.reason: Redrawn on 8 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing contradicted this text: it showed the athlete standing. Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 35 degrees so the wide elbows show: sitting at a low row station with the back upright, the feet on the plate and the knees slightly bent, arms straight toward the low pulley; the elbows lift high and wide and the rope comes to the neck until the hands are beside the ears and the upper arms are level, a pause, and a slower return to straight arms. The trunk and legs do not move. Not drawn: the palms-down grip.
entries.summary: Seated at a low cable row with the back upright, lift the elbows high and wide to pull the rope to the neck, hands beside the ears, pause, then return slowly to straight arms.

frames.caption: Sit at a low cable row station holding the rope ends with the palms facing down, back upright, knees slightly bent and arms straight in front.
Keeping the torso still, lift the elbows and pull the rope toward the neck until the hands are beside the ears and the upper arms are level with the floor.
Pause. Elbows high and wide.
Return slowly until the arms are straight.
Torso stays upright and still.

entries.name: Shotgun Row
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: standing at the low pulley, the hands reach long and the elbows drive back until the upper back finishes the pull at the ribs. Standard low-pulley setup chosen from the template; listed in the daily review. The hands now reach the body: the torso is the vertical line at x 44.5, and the pulling position comes to within 2.5 of it, against 5.5 before, so the frames named for reaching the ribs and the neck now actually do. The elbow is solved on the shoulder circle from the authored hand, so the upper arm (12.5) and forearm (12.0) hold their length by construction. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Six drawn positions of a shotgun row, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Reach into the start with long arms.
Drive the elbows back to begin the pull.
Elbows past the ribs; the upper back finishes.
Pause with the upper back engaged.
Return slowly along the same line.
Full reach again, ready for the next rep.

techniqueCitations: Haff, G. G., & Triplett, N. T. (Eds.). (2016). Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (4th ed.). Human Kinetics, pp. 396-397.
McGill, S. M. (2014). Ultimate Back Fitness and Performance (5th ed.). Backfitpro Inc., pp. 210-214.

frames.caption: Let the working arm reach long while the trunk stays braced and still.
Drive the elbow toward the hip, then lower to the full reach.
Cue: Drive the elbow toward the hip. Keep the torso square.
Lower smoothly back toward full reach.
If the torso rotates, reduce the load before shortening the row.

entries.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
entries.summary: Five drawn positions of a one-arm dumbbell row on a bench, seen from the side.
entries.instructions: Set up One-Arm Dumbbell Row with bench, dumbbells and choose a load or range you can control. Reach into the start, then drive the elbows back until the upper back finishes the pull. When the hands finish before the elbows, the load is too ambitious; reset and own the pull.
entries.cues: Set the torso before the pull. Lead with the elbows. Pause with the upper back engaged.
entries.coachingIntent: Train middle back with the specific loading and range of One-Arm Dumbbell Row while keeping each rep technically honest.
entries.reason: Derived from the Single-Arm Dumbbell Row authored joint path (derivesFrom 12): the library's One-Arm Dumbbell Row repeats the same bench-supported pull, so the drawn path is reused unchanged and only the text differs. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.

captionOverrides.reach-long-a-1: Brace on the bench and let the working arm hang long.
captionOverrides.elbow-drives-2: Pull by driving the elbow back toward the hip.
captionOverrides.elbow-to-the-3: Finish with the elbow at the hip and the upper back doing the work.
captionOverrides.lower-to-ful-4: Lower the bell under control to the full reach.
captionOverrides.full-stretch-5: If the torso turns or the shoulder shrugs, reset the rep.
